scope: M2-01 provider-neutral verified encrypted cloud backup core, Google Drive adapter contract and encrypted durable work orchestration
behavior: Only an envelope independently opened by the password and recovery key may become an upload artifact; credentials are not retained or passed to providers
A stable remote object is reserved before upload and the same backup ID cannot create a second remote object
An upload committed without a response is recovered by inspecting and matching remote metadata
Remote metadata and downloads are checked against SHA-256, byte length, content type, identity and creation time
Downloaded envelopes must still open through both credentials to the same payload
Authentication, permission, quota, throttling, availability and uncertain-result failures remain distinct
Google Drive pre-generated file IDs persist before upload; a committed 409 is recovered through metadata inspection instead of creating a duplicate
Verified envelopes are staged immutably and queued without retaining credentials or plaintext financial data
Staging, Drive object reservations and SQLCipher job state survive restart; reconciliation closes the stage-before-enqueue crash window
A crash after remote commit retries the same reserved Drive object, while tampered staging and same-ID different-content attempts fail closed
A registry supports multiple provider adapters without a hard-coded default and exposes history only for providers that implement the catalog capability
Retention produces a deterministic keep/delete preview, keeps at least one backup, can protect recent backups and performs no deletion until explicitly applied
Retention refreshes all candidate metadata before applying; the Drive adapter inspects each file again immediately before permanent deletion
The app-facing manual flow routes by provider ID, double-verifies an upload before scheduling and exposes provider-neutral history/retention use cases
A downloaded envelope is transport-verified and then unlocks with either its password or recovery key; rejected credentials remain distinct from corrupt remote bytes
A standalone provider-neutral Flutter screen supports create, history, password/recovery restore handoff and retention with explicit permanent-deletion confirmation
The Flutter screen maps authentication, quota, throttling, credential and integrity failures without exposing secrets
The Google Drive REST transport implements generateIds, trusted resumable upload, metadata, download, complete paginated history and permanent deletion
Bearer token header injection, untrusted upload locations, repeated page tokens and oversized histories fail closed; post-byte network/308/408/5xx outcomes remain uncertain for same-ID inspection
HTTP 401, permission, quota, throttling, conflict, availability and uncertain-result failures retain distinct meanings
Authentication, permission, quota and integrity failures stop automatic retries; throttling, availability, uncertain result and temporary local failures retain bounded backoff
A user-action retry keeps the same backup ID and reservation, while encrypted work schema 1 upgrades to schema 2 without losing staged work
Encrypted automatic schedules are opt-in, start at the next selected period and derive a stable occurrence backup ID
A crash after staging reuses the same automatic occurrence, missed periods coalesce to one backup and unresolved uploads block pile-up
